titulo: Secure MCP server: audience, minimum scope, handle tied to the user, and secret kept out of the repo
lead: You built the server's OAuth in course 1. Here is the other side: six attacks from the MCP security list (revision 2026-07-28) against the same server, written two ways. You see what the official SDK blocks on its own and what it only blocks if you configure it.
objetivo: run 6 attacks against a weak MCP server and a secure one, and separate what the SDK blocks on its own from what depends on your configuration.

aprende.t: Host and Origin: DNS rebinding against a local server
Token only in the header, with an expiry and for this server (audience)
Minimum scope at the door, and the action's scope only when it is requested
No session in MCP 2026-07-28: the state handle is not a login

hero_alt: A small server in a rack with a physical padlock and a network cable plugged in, on a dark desk under neutral light.

secoes.titulo: The five gates of a request
secoes.sub: A request to the server passes through these gates, in this order. Click each one.

nos.detalhe: An outside page can talk to a server on 127.0.0.1 through DNS rebinding. The localhostHostValidation and localhostOriginValidation guards from @modelcontextprotocol/node refuse with 403 before anything else. You turn them on.
The SDK only reads Authorization: Bearer; a token in the URL does not get in (the spec forbids query strings). A token with no expiry or an expired one: 401. The SDK does this.
The spec says: "MCP servers MUST NOT accept any tokens that were not explicitly issued for the MCP server". In the SDK this only happens if you pass expectedResource. You turn it on.

Signing in asks only for mentorias:ler. The action asks for mentorias:agendar with scopeChallenge: requireScopes(...), and the 403 carries the missing scope (step-up). You declare it, the SDK does it.

Revision 2026-07-28 has no session. The draft, the cart or the flow has a handle that comes back as an argument. Having the handle is not being logged in: check the owner through the token. You write this.

secoes.legenda: Checked against the code of @modelcontextprotocol/server 2.3.1 (dist/) and the security_best_practices page of revision 2026-07-28.

secoes.sub: The same server with the common mistakes: it accepts a token in the URL, does not check the audience, does not ask for a scope on the action, and uses a sequential handle with no owner. Tokens are generated on the fly; nothing in the repository.

abas.html:
== @modelcontextprotocol/server 2.3.1 · MCP 2026-07-28 · servidor: fraco
bloqueado 1 · Host de fora (DNS rebinding) → HTTP 401 (o token barrou; servidor sem token cairia)
PASSOU    2 · token na query string → aceito
PASSOU    3 · token de outro recurso → aceito
PASSOU    4 · escopo de leitura confirma agendamento → agendado: m-101 para ana
PASSOU    5 · handle de outro usuário → agendado: m-102 para ana
bloqueado 6 · token vencido → invalid_token: Token has expired
passaram: 4 de 6
saída: 1

Attack 1 stopped at the token: a local server with no token would fall. The SDK always blocks 6. The four in the middle depend on you.

secoes.sub: The differences are marked with seguro in the server file.

abas.html:
== @modelcontextprotocol/server 2.3.1 · MCP 2026-07-28 · servidor: seguro
bloqueado 1 · Host de fora (DNS rebinding) → HTTP 403 (Host recusado antes do token)
bloqueado 2 · token na query string → invalid_token: Missing Authorization header
bloqueado 3 · token de outro recurso → invalid_token: Token was not issued for this resource
bloqueado 4 · escopo de leitura confirma agendamento → Insufficient scope: required "mentorias:agendar"
bloqueado 5 · handle de outro usuário → rascunho não encontrado
bloqueado 6 · token vencido → invalid_token: Token has expired
passaram: 0 de 6
saída: 0

Each refusal comes from a different place: Host (the Node adapter's guard), token and audience (the SDK, with expectedResource), scope (requireScopes), handle (your code).

texto: Reads the token from the header only, rejects a token that has no expiry or has expired, and responds 403 with the missing scope when the tool declares requireScopes.
expectedResource (audience), the Host and Origin guards, the server on 127.0.0.1, and the scope per tool. A local server that only your agent uses: stdio, which doesn't even open a port.
A random handle (randomBytes) tied to the token's user. The spec: "MUST NOT treat possession of a state handle as authentication".

Pass the client's token on to another API (token passthrough, forbidden by the spec) or keep a secret in a file in the repository. The client also keeps credentials per issuer and doesn't reuse them with another authorization server (a change in the 2026-07-28 version).

secoes.sub: A minimal checker (it does not replace gitleaks or GitHub's secret scanning). The second command plants a fake key in a rehearsal folder so you can see it get flagged.

blocos.conteudo:
cd ~/projetos/formacao-webmcp-seguranca-v72/kit
node scripts/segredos.mjs .; echo "saída: $?"
E=${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ensaio-seguranca/vazou; mkdir -p $E
printf "export const API_KEY = '%s';\n" $(openssl rand -hex 16) > $E/config.mjs
node scripts/segredos.mjs $E; echo "saída: $?"

abas.html:
70 arquivos lidos · 0 segredos
saída: 0
SEGREDO config.mjs:1: segredo atribuído no código (API_KEY = 'a…)
1 arquivo lido · 1 segredo
saída: 1

The kit passes clean; the rehearsal folder flags the key written in the code.

exercicios.texto: Run the fraco block and note which four attacks got through.
Run the seguro block. Then, in mcp/servidor.mjs, remove expectedResource from secure mode and run it again. Undo it at the end.
exercicios.pronto: passaram: 0 de 6; without expectedResource, PASSOU 3 · token de outro recurso.

exercicios.texto: Run the checker on the repository of your server or site.

perguntas.p: A token issued for another service from the same provider reaches your server. In SDK 2.3.1, what makes it get rejected?
opcoes: Nothing: the SDK always rejects a token from another service
The Host and Origin guard of the Node adapter, on by default
The expectedResource you pass to requireBearerAuth
The requireScopes declared on the read tool
perguntas.explica: The SDK only compares the audience if you configure expectedResource (and the verifier returns resource). Attack 3 got through on the weak server because of that.

perguntas.p: Bruno sends the code for Ana's draft and confirms the booking. Which MCP 2026-07-28 rule does this break?
opcoes: Having the state handle is not authentication
The token must come in the header
The server must respond to server/discover
perguntas.explica: With no session in the protocol, state lives in handles. The server checks the owner through the token, never through possession of the handle.

perguntas.p: Which of these does the SDK do without you configuring anything?
opcoes: Check that the token was issued for this server
Reject an outside Host to block DNS rebinding
Generate random handles for the drafts
Ignore a token sent in the URL query string
perguntas.explica: verifyBearerToken only reads the Authorization header. You turn on audience and Host; you write the handle.

perguntas.p: Why does the kit's server ask only for mentorias:ler to get in?
opcoes: Because the SDK doesn't accept more than one scope in the same token
So the ordinary token can't book: the action asks for its own scope
Because a write scope only exists on the stdio transport
To let the client skip the consent screen
perguntas.explica: Minimum scope at sign-in, and the action's scope only when it is requested. A leaked read token can't book anything.

itens.texto: Header, expiry and declared scope: it handles those.
Audience, Host/Origin, a handle with an owner, and no passthrough.
In the environment, never in the repository; check before you publish.
